rawOutput.rationale: Start with a simple WWI cause map, then move through outbreak sequence and basic chronology with alternating teach and retrieve steps.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions made the July Crisis dangerous and gave leaders reasons to expect support or fear isolation.
The Sarajevo assassination triggered the July Crisis, and decisions by Austria-Hungary, Germany, Russia, France, and Britain turned a regional crisis into declarations of war.
From 1914 to 1918, the war expanded, the United States entered later, and the armistice ended the fighting in 1918.
completionEvidence: Name the main alliance blocs and at least three prewar tensions from the model.
Put Sarajevo, the July Crisis, the start of the war, U.S. entry, and the armistice in the correct order.
Classify each major event as a cause, outbreak step, or chronology marker.

methodBriefing.name: Feynman Technique
methodBriefing.what: Study a short model, explain it in your own words, fix any gap, then explain it again without copying.
methodBriefing.why: It helps turn a big picture into a connected story and exposes missing links early.
how: Say the idea back in plain language.
Compare your answer with the model and repair one gap.
Explain it again more clearly and more completely.
methodBriefing.completion: You complete the method when you can explain the cause map and chronology clearly in your own words after repair.
personalization: Keep one step visible at a time.
Expect a hint before the full correction if needed.

activities.label: Alliance map
activities.title: Alliance map before 1914
activities.body: Read the model and note the main relationships. Then be ready to explain them in your own words.

essentialIdeas: Prewar European alliances and tensions made the July Crisis dangerous and gave leaders reasons to expect support or fear isolation.

activities.label: Explain the buildup
activities.title: Why the crisis spread
activities.body: In one or two paragraphs, explain how the assassination became a wider war. Then compare your wording with the model.
activities.concept: The Sarajevo assassination triggered the July Crisis, and decisions by Austria-Hungary, Germany, Russia, France, and/or:
activities.correctAnswer: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand triggered the July Crisis, and the alliance commitments and mobilization decisions of Austria-Hungary, Germany, Russia, France, and Britain turned it into declarations of war.
activities.feedback: A complete answer links the assassination to the July Crisis and shows how decisions by major powers widened the conflict into war.

activities.label: Fix the sequence
activities.title: Repair the outbreak sequence
activities.body: Use the cue from the last answer to correct one missing link. Then give a shorter corrected version.
activities.concept: The Sarajevo assassination triggered the July Crisis, and decisions by Austria-Hungary, Germany, Russia, France, and/or:
activities.correctAnswer: After the Sarajevo assassination, Austria-Hungary moved against Serbia, Germany backed Austria-Hungary, Russia mobilized, and the alliance reactions led to declarations of war.
activities.feedback: The repair should include the step-by-step chain from assassination to wider mobilization and declarations of war, not just the assassination itself.

activities.label: Timeline from memory
activities.title: WWI timeline in order
activities.body: Explain the war from 1914 to 1918 from memory in a clear sequence. Keep it brief and chronological.
activities.concept: From 1914 to 1918, the war expanded, the United States entered later, and the armistice ended the fighting in 1918.
activities.correctAnswer: The war began in 1914, expanded into a larger conflict, the United States entered in 1917, and the armistice ended the fighting in 1918.
activities.feedback: A complete chronology includes the start year, the later U.S. entry, and the armistice as the end point.

activities.label: Check the full map
activities.title: Build the WWI map
activities.body: Choose the best summary of the cause map. Then check whether it matches the whole story.
choices: Prewar alliances and tensions made the July Crisis dangerous, the Sarajevo assassination helped trigger the outbreak, and the war ran from 1914 to 1918 with U.S. entry in 1917 and the armistice in 1918.
The war began because the United States entered first, and the armistice happened before the major alliances mattered.
The Sarajevo assassination ended the war immediately, so the rest of the timeline is only background.
World War I was mainly a short local conflict in 1914 with no later expansion or armistice in 1918.
activities.correctAnswer: Prewar alliances and tensions made the July Crisis dangerous, the Sarajevo assassination helped trigger the outbreak, and the war ran from 1914 to 1918 with U.S. entry in 1917 and the armistice in 1918.
activities.feedback: The correct summary connects causes, outbreak sequence, and the basic timeline in one chain.

activities.label: Return point
activities.title: Come back to the timeline
activities.body: Write one sentence about what still feels uncertain. Then stop here and return to this timeline later.

items.essentialIdea: Prewar European alliances and tensions divided Europe into rival alliance blocs before 1914.

check.title: Alliance blocs before 1914
check.prompt: How did prewar European alliances shape the balance of power before 1914?
check.referenceAnswer: Europe was split into rival alliance blocs that increased tension and made a wider war more likely.
check.feedback: It is about opposing blocs creating instability, not a single alliance or a later wartime alliance shift.

items.essentialIdea: The Sarajevo assassination triggered the crisis that led from Austria-Hungary's ultimatum to war declarations.

check.title: From murder to war
check.prompt: What sequence connected the Sarajevo assassination to the first war declarations?
check.referenceAnswer: The assassination in Sarajevo led Austria-Hungary to issue an ultimatum, then declarations of war followed as allies mobilized.
check.feedback: It connects the assassination to the diplomatic crisis, not just to one immediate declaration.

items.essentialIdea: Basic chronology from 1914 to 1918 places World War I from outbreak to armistice.

check.title: World War I dates
check.prompt: What is the basic chronology of World War I from 1914 to 1918?
check.referenceAnswer: World War I began in 1914 and ended in 1918 with the armistice.
check.feedback: The key relationship is start in 1914 and end in 1918, not later peace settlements.

The outbreak of fighting in 1914
recognitionCheck.feedback: It began the crisis chain before the war itself.
